note: Spec pass 2026-10-15: groupings by an agent from the claims it read. The first hub reuses the procedural-learning spec's question verbatim; its evidence is reading-strategy instruction (Duffy 1987, Paris 1983), with the mathematics coming from the members (Rittle-Johnson & Star 2007 inside the comparison claim, Star 2015 practice guide). The second hub is the only claim that runs explicit word-problem strategy instruction and measures the result (Stein 1998, one class, no control); the Polya/Dahmus claims are one study (Bassler 1972) comparing two strategies, and the formatted-plan claim is Zambo 1994.

findings.question: Does teaching when and why to use a procedure, not only its steps, improve flexible use and understanding?
Does explicitly teaching a strategy or plan for word problems improve how learners set up and solve them?
